senses.gloss: Subabhru = Kṛshṇa: XII, 1511.
Subāhu^1, a serpent. § 47 (Sarpasattra): I, 35, 1559 (enumeration).--§ 564 (Mātalīyop.): V, 103, 3632 (do.),
Subāhu^2, an Apsaras. § 103 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 65, 2558 (daughter of Prādhā).--§ 191 (Arjuna): I, 123, 4819 (among the Apsarases who danced at the birth of Arjuna).

Subāhu^3, various kings at the time of Yudhishṭhira. § 130 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 67, 2660 (incarnation of the Asura Hara), 2696 (among the incarnations from the Krodhavaśa gaṇa).-§ 554 (Sainyodyogap.): V, 4, 77. Cf. Subāhu^5, Subāhu^8--9.

Subāhu^4, son of Dhṛtarāshṭra. § 130. (Aṃśāvat.): I, 67, 2729.--§ 182 (Dhṛtarāshṭraputranāmak.): I, 117, 4542.-§ 209 (Drupadaśāsana): I, 138, 5461.--§ 585 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 96, 4349 (among other sons of Dhṛtarāshṭra defeated by Bhīmasena).--§ 592 (Saṃśaptakavadhap.): VII, 25, 1077 (protected Droṇa against his brother Yuyutsu).-§ 596 (Pratijñāp.): VII, 74, 2629(?).--§ 600 (Ghaṭotkacavadhap.): VII, 170, 7671.--§ 608 (Karṇap.): VIII, 51, 2447 (among twenty sons of Dhṛtarāshṭra who attacked Bhīmasena).
Subāhu^5, a Kāśi king. § 280 (Bhīmasena): II, 30, 1080 (Kāśirājaṃ, vanquished by Bhīmasena on his digvijaya).
Subāhu^6, a Cedi king at the time of Nala. § 347 (Nalopākhyānap.): III, 64, 2531 (Cedīrājasya); 65, 2576 (do.). Cf. Cedipati, Cedirāja.

Subāhu^7, king of the Kulindas. § 419 (Gandhamādanapr.): III, 140, 10863 (ºvishayaṃ, on Himavat, description), 10865 (Kulindānām īśvaraḥ).--§ 449 (Ājagarap.): III, 177, †12349 (Kirātarājño vishayaṃ Sºoḥ), †12351 (ºvishaye), †12352. Cf. Kirātarājan, Kulindādhipati.
Subāhu^8, a Kuru warrior. § 592 (Saṃśaptakavadhap.): VII, 18, 738, 740, 741 (among the Saṃśaptakas, fought with Arjuna).--§ 609 (Śalyap.): IX, 2, 76 (had sided with Duryodhana).
Subāhu^9, a Pāṇḍava warrior. § 597 (Pratijñāp.): VII, 83, 2951.
Subāhu^10, a warrior of Skanda. § 615u (Skanda): IX, 45, 2575.
Subāhu^11, an ancient king. § 761 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 115, 5668 (among the kings who abstained from meat during the month of Kārttika).
Subandhanavimocana, Subāndhava = Śiva (1000 names^2).
Subala^1, an ancient king. § 6 (Anukram.): I, 1, 229 (in Sañjaya's enumeration).

Subala^2, king of the Gāndhāras and father of Śakuni and Gāndhārī. § 83 (Ādivaṃśāvatāraṇa): I, 63, 2439 (Nagnajit?, disciple of Prahrāda).--§ 174 (Dhṛtarāshtravivāha): I, 110, 4367 (ºsyātmajā, i.e. Gāndhārī), 4373 (Gāndhārarājasya, gave his daughter Gāndhārī in marriage to Dhṛtarāshṭra).--§ 287 (Rājasūyikap.): II, 34, 1265 (Gāndhārarājaḥ, came to the rājasūya of Yudhishṭhira).--§ 292 (do.): II, 45, 1608 (accompanied by Nakula).--§ 327 (Draupadīparitāpav.): III, 34, †1356 (ºsya putraḥ, i.e. Śakuni).--§ 569 (Bhagavadyānap.): V, 148, †5031 (ºsya putrī, i.e. Gāndhārī).-§ 585 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 90, 4004 (ºsyātmajāḥ, i.e. Gaja, etc.), 4009 (ºsyātmajān = do.).--§ 611 (Śalyap.): IX, 22, 1153 (ºsya sutaḥ, i.e. Śakuni); 28, 1558 (ºsya putraḥ, i.e. Śakuni), †1561 (do., do.).--§ 612 (Hradapraveśap.) IX, 29, 1600 (ºsya hate putre, i.e. Śakuni). Cf. Gāndhārarāja.
Subala^3, a king. § 522 (Draupadīharaṇap.): III, 265, †15596 (Ikshvākurājñaḥ Sº sya putraḥ, followed Jayadratha, only C., B. has Subhavasya).
Subala^4, a Suparṇa, son of Garuḍa. § 564 (Mātalīyop.): V, 101, 3588 (enumeration).
Subala^5 = Śiva (1000 names^2).
Subaladāyāda (“the son of Subala”) = Kālikeya: VII, 1933 (Kº),
Subalaja = Śakuni, q.v.
Subalajā = Gāndhārī, q.v.
Subalaputra, Subalatmaja = Śakuni, q.v.
Subalātmajā = Gāndhārī, q.v.

Subalātmaja, pl. (ºāḥ) (“the sons of Subala^2”). § 585 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 90, 4011 (i.e. Gaja, Gavākska, Vṛshabha, Carmavat, Ārjava, and Śuka), 4013 (do., except Vṛshabha they are slain by Irāvat).
Subīja = Śiva (1000 names^2).
